description.value: Boya Lake is celebrated across BC for its vivid turquoise water, making this 44-site developed park on the Cassiar Highway a genuine Stikine Region destination; potable water and washrooms are on-site, but the gate closes on first snowfall so timing is everything.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM tags are the primary evidence source here, as the fetched website content is almost entirely navigation menu boilerplate with no park-specific amenity details. OSM tags directly confirm drinking_water=yes, shower=no, toilets=yes, laundry=no, reservation=yes, and power_supply=no. The BC Parks website confirms the campground is real and open, but also reveals a name discrepancy: the official name is 'Tā Ch'ilā Park [a.k.a. Boya Lake Park]', not 'Boya Lake Provincial Campground' as in OSM.
concerns: Name mismatch: OSM lists 'Boya Lake Provincial Campground' but the official BC Parks website identifies the park as 'Tā Ch'ilā Park [a.k.a. Boya Lake Park]'.
The contact email (lookingtwice@gmail.com) belongs to the private operator 'Looking Twice', not BC Parks — cyclists may be better directed to the BC Parks website for reservations.
Fetched website content was almost entirely site-wide navigation; park-specific amenity details were not captured, limiting website-based verification.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, operating BC Parks provincial campground on a major touring route; confirmed open via the official BC Parks website.
enrichment_extras.notes: Located on Highway 37 (Stewart-Cassiar Highway) with no mobile reception; cyclists should plan provisions and communications accordingly. OSM lists internet_access=no and mobile_reception=no.

wow_evidence: celebrated across BC for its vivid turquoise water... genuine Stikine Region destination; potable water and washrooms are on-site
